action: General advice: Expedia customers should be cautious with emails or texts about bookings or refunds, use a unique password with two-step login, and watch for an official Expedia statement.
exec: A very large but unverified data theft claim against a major travel platform, said to involve a third-party provider.
plain: A criminal group claims to hold nearly one billion Expedia traveller records taken through an outside supplier. Expedia confirmed a breach at that supplier but not the group's numbers.

evidence.quote: Expedia investigates cyberattack after hackers claim theft of nearly 1 billion customer records

summary: A Russian-speaking extortion group calling itself n0n claims to hold nearly one billion Expedia traveler records taken through a compromised third-party data platform provider. Expedia confirmed attackers reached its systems via that provider but told The Seattle Times the hackers' claims are unverified and it could not confirm their accuracy; its investigation continues. A law firm is weighing a possible class action, The Seattle Times reported.
title: Extortion group claims theft of nearly one billion Expedia traveler records

validation.note: Attacker claim reported by Security Affairs, Valley News Live and MyNorthwest; Expedia's statements (to Skift and The Seattle Times, as relayed) confirm a third-party provider compromise but not n0n's figures.

review.note: Security Affairs says Expedia confirmed a breach via a third-party data platform provider but not n0n's figures; summary/plain/action said no confirmation found. Fixed; status stays claimed sev 1; correction filed.
